GraceUXGuidelines.Audience: One human user interacting through Telegram, Web, MCP, and future channel adapters.
GraceUXGuidelines.Guideline: Use human-facing labels for materials, selections, runs, results, errors, downloads, and retention; keep internal IDs and execution vocabulary out of ordinary Web and Telegram copy.
Adapters present API-owned lifecycle truth and preserve restart-safe channel surfaces; a channel surface must not mutate product lifecycle implicitly.
Show accepted, pending, running, partial, failed, canceled, and unavailable states with stable diagnostics and actionable recovery where supported.
Maintain ordered selection behavior and explicit user actions; later inbox arrivals remain visible after a processing launch detaches only the captured membership.
Keep normal Telegram and Web flows provider-agnostic; expose CopperASR run-manifest metadata only through explicit service-artifact/MCP requests.
Telegram copy and action labels are Russian-first; collection actions, processing launch, cancellation, retry, results, and recovery must remain explicit.
Successful Telegram processing results are delivered immediately and recorded as result_artifact_surface evidence; a Result button is not the normal delivery path.
New YouTube M4A/AAC audio exports render as native music cards with bounded title, performer, and duration; legacy OGG/Opus stays voice, generic audio stays audio, and non-audio stays document.

Web must not make media_asset, selection_snapshot, analysis_run_step, channel_surface, Run builder, Artifacts, Diagnostics, Run manifest, Analysis run, Media item, opaque identifiers, or raw diagnostic internals load-bearing terms outside explicit admin/debug views.
